answer.rationale:
Constraints first: rollback_release is off the table (compliance bars reverting the security patch), so memory_b1's success record is irrelevant here regardless of how good it looks. regional_failover (memory_b2) restored latency in March, but that was a latency degradation, not a settlement peak with heavy in-flight writes; shifting regions mid-peak risks exactly the failure mode the primary objective forbids — losing customer writes. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) worked for a partner dependency outage where failing fast was cheap; here failing fast on the write path means shedding settlement writes, which is a direct objective violation. That leaves the two non-destructive levers. route_read_replicas is my intent because it relieves the primary without touching write durability and can be scoped narrowly, and add_capacity is the fallback if verification undercuts it.

Why verify b5 and b3 specifically: these are the only two memories still live in my decision, and both carry a plausible mismatch to today's conditions. memory_b5 recorded write latency recovering after report queries moved off the primary — but if the original record shows the primary was dashboard/read-saturated rather than write-saturated, the mechanism does not transfer to a write-path bottleneck at settlement peak, and I would be pattern-matching on the outcome rather than the cause. memory_b3 recorded headroom absorbing a retail promotional surge — a forecast-ahead provisioning action, not a 90-minute-in mitigation; if the source shows capacity was added before the window rather than during it, add_capacity is not actually available to me as a live intervention and the fallback collapses.

Downstream value risk: these memories are consolidated summaries that record what worked, not the conditions under which it worked, and every one of them reads as a success. That asymmetry is itself a warning — a memory store of wins will make any of these five look safe, and the p99 climb has a cause I have not identified. Nothing in the inherited record tells me whether the new release is contributing to write latency even though it cannot be reverted; that unknown survives this action.

Scale: small_guarded_test. I am routing only clearly-identifiable report/dashboard query classes off the primary, with write-loss monitoring and an explicit abort if p99 does not respond, rather than a broad read-traffic reroute. A guarded slice preserves the one intervention window's information value if the b5 mechanism turns out not to apply, instead of spending it on a broad move justified by a summary I have not yet confirmed.
